# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver, Income & Protection Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built 100% live from official New Zealand Crown and statutory releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Jonathan Palliser, FSP1004725), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Media Kit & Citation Guide: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations | HLF Glossary: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/tools/glossary
> Reuse Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for HLF-derived figures & commentary; official statistics credited to their respective publishers.
> Date Standard: Observation Period (latest monthly: September 2026) | Period End | Source Publication Date | Last Checked (16 November 2026 / 2026-11-16).
> Active datasets: 62.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Reality Check Benchmarks (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/
- Media Kit & Citation Guide (HTML): https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (62 Active Datasets)
- [Existing 'back-book' effective mortgage rate vs newly settled fixed mortgage rates (RBNZ Table B6 vs B30) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/back-book-vs-new-settled-mortgage-rate/): In September 2026, the effective interest rate paid across all existing New Zealand bank mortgages ('back book', RBNZ Table B6) averaged 4.81%, compared with 4.82% for newly settled 1-year fixed owner-occupier loans (RBNZ Table B30)—a difference of 1 basis points (-0.01%). [Official Data: RBNZ Table B6 & B30 (September 2026): Existing housing loan book yield = 4.81%; New settled 1-year fixed rate = 4.82%. | HLF Calculation: Existing Housing Loan Yield (Table B6) = 4.81% vs 1Y Newly Settled Rate (Table B30) = 4.82% (Spread = -1 bps) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Existing 'back-book' effective mortgage rate vs newly settled fixed mortgage rates (RBNZ Table B6 vs B30)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Yields on Loans (Table B6) & New Residential Mortgage Weighted Average Interest Rates (Table B30). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/back-book-vs-new-settled-mortgage-rate/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps). | HLF Calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after reference quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, the cost of purchasing a newly built home changed by +3.2% year-on-year, compared with 3.7% headline CPI inflation. [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Purchase of newly built home = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI)," September 2026 quarter. - [Personal & consumer loan borrower stress: non-performing consumer loans & NPL ratio (RBNZ Table S50) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-loan-stress-npl/): In September 2026, New Zealand bank non-performing personal and consumer loans (90+ days past due or impaired) stood at 0.90% ($66m) (down from 1.1% a year earlier). [Official Data: RBNZ Table S50 (September 2026): Bank non-performing consumer loans = $66m (0.90% of consumer lending). | HLF Calculation: Non-Performing Bank Consumer Loans = $66m (0.90% of consumer loan book; vs 1.10% a year earlier) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-personal-lending-stock/): As at September 2026, total New Zealand personal and consumer lending (personal loans, vehicle finance, hire purchase, overdrafts, and cards) stood at $14.64B ($14,636m) (up 2.2% year-on-year from $14.32B a year earlier), including $7.33B (50.1%) from non-bank lenders. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C5 (September 2026): Total consumer sector lending stock = $14,636m ($14.64B). | HLF Calculation: Total NZ Consumer Lending = $14,636m ($14.64B; YoY: +2.2%) | Non-Bank Share: $7,332m ÷ $14,636m = 50.1% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5)," September 2026. - [New Zealand credit card debt, share accruing interest & weighted average interest rate (RBNZ Table C12) (Obs: August 2026 | End: 2026-08-31 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/credit-card-balances-interest-share/): In August 2026, New Zealanders owed $5.38B ($5,378m) in credit card balances (down 1.9% year-on-year from $5,481m a year earlier), with 51.3% ($2,758m) accruing interest at a weighted average rate of 20.0% p.a.. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C12 (August 2026): Total credit card advances outstanding = $5,378m ($5.38B). | HLF Calculation: Total Card Advances = $5,378m ($5.38B) | Interest-Bearing: $2,758m ÷ $5,378m = 51.3% at 20.0% p.a. | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [First-home buyer high Debt-to-Income (>6x DTI) share vs 20% RBNZ speed limit (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/dti-headroom/): In September 2026, 9.0% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($137.0m of $1,525.0m)—sitting 11.0 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $137.0m out of $1,525.0m total FHB commitments. | HLF Calculation: $137.0m ÷ $1,525.0m = 9.0% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.0% = 11.0 pts) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up lending value = $962m across 9,639 borrowers. | HLF Calculation: Reported $962m top-up lending × $1m ÷ 9,639 borrowers = $99,803 mean | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Median equivalised household disposable income before & after housing costs (Stats NZ HILS) (Obs: Year ended June 2025 | End: 2025-06-30 | Published: Annual Stats NZ Household Income and Housing-Cost Statistics release)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/equivalised-household-income-family-size/): In the year ended june 2025, New Zealand's median equivalised household disposable income was $60,521 before housing costs and $45,645 after deducting housing costs—meaning housing outgoings absorbed 24.6% ($14,876/year per equivalised adult) of disposable income. [Official Data: Stats NZ HILS (Year ended June 2025): Median equivalised disposable income BHC = $60,521; AHC = $45,645. | HLF Calculation: Median Equivalised Disposable Income: $60,521 Before Housing Costs (BHC) vs $45,645 After Housing Costs (AHC; 24.6% housing deduction) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [First-home buyers with a 20%+ deposit (<=80% LVR) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): In September 2026, 49.7% of first-home buyers (1,325 borrowers, or $680m in lending) purchased with a 20% or greater deposit (&le;80% LVR), with an average mortgage size of $513,208. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,325 <=80% LVR FHB borrowers ($680m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers. | HLF Calculation: 1,325 ÷ 2,667 = 49.7% (Mean loan: $680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals & lending total (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Over the 12 months to September 2026, 33,485 first-home buyers were approved for mortgages totalling $19.61B ($19,613m) across New Zealand (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 borrowers (47.0%) purchasing with under a 20% deposit (&gt;80% LVR). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (12 months to September 2026): Sum of monthly FHB approvals = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR FHB approvals = 15,743 loans. | HLF Calculation: 12-month sum = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR share = 15,743 ÷ 33,485 = 47.0% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals & lending total," September 2026. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): Total FHB new lending = $1,530m (LVRN.MMB1.AC1) across 2,667 FHB loans (LVRN.MMB2.AC1). | HLF Calculation: ($1,530m × $1,000,000) ÷ 2,667 loans = $573,678 | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory.
